actionable_improvement: among the latest 20 successful docs.yml runs in the last 14 days, docs execution spent a median 44s in build and 54s end-to-end, with dashboard restore itself only 2.0s median. Trusted docs logs confirmed repeated cache hits for the central-agentic-ops-dashboard cache and node_modules, so docs is already reusing the dashboard artifact efficiently. However, trusted cao-dashboard runs that feed that cache still spend 54-59s in Upgrade fallback activity data on every successful push while the actual Assemble Dashboard Language site step takes only 1-5s and artifact upload 7-8s. Those same logs validated and recopied a 361.1 MiB gh-aw-logs.sqlite plus 103 shards / 228.5 MiB into the reusable dashboard artifact before compressing ~34.7 MiB for upload. This makes reusable dashboard generation bottleneck on rebuilding and repackaging the activity database instead of on dashboard rendering. A workflow change that publishes and reuses a pre-upgraded, ready-to-package dashboard input (or otherwise skips Upgrade fallback activity data when the restored activity cache already validates) is expected to save about 55s per cao-dashboard run, which is roughly 57% of that workflow's build job and would remove the dominant source feeding docs dashboard freshness.
